newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-TROUBLED MOOD IN DORTMUND CAMP BEFORE EUROPEAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUBLED MOOD IN DORTMUND CAMP BEFORE EUROPEAN FINAL.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's failure to qualify directly for next season's Champions' League will give the Germans extra motivation for Wednesday's European Cup final against Juventus.

A 2-1 defeat at lowly Hamburg at the weekend ended Dortmund's slim hopes of stopping new champions Bayern Munich and second-placed Bayer Leverkusen from taking the Bundesliga's two spots in next season's European Cup.

Only a victory over favourites Juventus in Munich's Olympic stadium will ensure a place in the lucrative Champions' League for the 1995 and 1996 German champions whose form slipped in the crucial run-in to the title race.

"We are obviously disappointed that we did not win the championship and have missed out on second place," coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "But we are going to be concentrating hard on Wednesday. If we have a good day, we can win it."
Midfielder Andy Moeller admitted: "The spirit in the team has suffered a bit of a setback after we didn't win the championship."

Dortmund's position contrasts sharply with Juventus who are sure of their place in the competition next season after clinching their 24th Italian league championship on Friday with a 1-1 draw with Atalanta.
There are certainly signs of problems in the German camp which may boil over if Dortmund lose.
There has been speculation that their injury-plagued European footballer-of-the-year Matthias Sammer might leave the club or even quit the game.
Libero Sammer, who has struggled with injuries all season, has been very disappointed by the way he has been treated in public during a tough time in recent months.
But Hitzfeld said: "I can't imagine that he will finish his career. He will carry on."
Chairman Gerd Niebaum, however, conceded the mood in the German camp was far from perfect.
"At the moment there is a great deal of frustration because we have not achieved our goals for the season," Niebaum said.
Nevertheless, Dortmund prepared to fly to Munich on Monday with few injuries worries. Moeller is fit again after a calf injury and striker Karlheinz Riedle has recovered from a shin problem.

By contrast Juventus and Yugoslavia midfielder Vladimir Jugovic is worried that too many people are taking it for granted that the Italians will beat the Germans in the Olympic stadium which staged the 1974 World Cup final.
"This is a big match build-up that leaves me relaxed and worried at the same time and that's not a contradiction," he said.
"People around us, the fans all seem to think that it is a mere formality for us and that is not a psychologically favourable situation.
